correctness.rationale: For each nontrivial H-arm orbit O_j with size t_j, invariance forces exactly the same finite set of positive radii in every arm in O_j. Each radius uses t_j particles. Because a nonsingleton orbit cannot coalesce at the common center without collision, its occupied-radius count a_j is locally constant. Removing those orbit points leaves an arbitrary unordered configuration on S_f. Conversely the center/fixed-arm configuration plus strictly ordered independent radial lists P_{a_j} reconstructs a unique H-fixed unordered configuration, continuously in each clopen stratum. P_a is convex; all UConf_n(S_f) are connected (interval for f<=2, graph-spine for f>=3). Summing strata gives b0 generating function. Farley-Sabalka established the star graph first Betti formula R_f(n)=1+(f-2)C(n+f-2,f-1)-C(n+f-2,f-2), n>=0, f>=3. Its ordinary generating function is ((1-z)^{f-1}-1+(f-1)z)/(1-z)^f; multiplying by the orbit-radius Hilbert series gives the announced b1. With f=0 only center residual counts n=0 or1, giving (1+z) times orbit series. All high integral homology vanishes as star factors retract to graphs. Boundary k=0, f=0, f=1,2, singleton orbits, and all H are covered. Five-arm single transposition k=4 yields ranks 6,1,0 across three components, consistent with direct formula and frozen checker. Graph-spine test source inspected (245 parameter cases); these are corroboration, while proof is radial rigidity plus cited ordinary star theorem.
